nodes.notes: GET https://service-a.example.com/healthz — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Combine Probe Results
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: All Healthy?

nodes.name: Already Alerted? (State Check)
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

# Alert the team on new events: Notion & Gmail

**Pattern:** Event Notification · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers integrations work end to end across Notion, Gmail, Slack and Google Sheets.

It moves through 29 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Probe Endpoint A
3. Probe Endpoint B
4. Combine Probe Results
5. All Healthy?
6. Record Uptime Metric
7. Already Alerted? (State Check)
8. Page On-Call via Gmail
9. Load Previous Snapshot
10. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
11. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
12. Archive Row Snapshot
13. Stamp Completion Time
14. Persist Run Metadata
15. Fingerprint for Idempotency
16. Drop Already-Processed Items
17. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
18. Record Sub-workflow Result
19. Enrich with Reference Data
20. Fold In Enrichment Fields
21. Tag Pipeline Metadata
22. Save Execution Metadata
23. Sort Jobs Newest First
24. Align Field Names
25. Stamp Processing Time
26. Cap Batch Volume
27. Summarize Run Stats
28. Append Audit Row (Notion)
29. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing integrations work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Probe Endpoint A → Probe Endpoint B → Combine Probe Results → All Healthy? → Record Uptime Metric → Already Alerted? (State Check) → Page On-Call via Gmail → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Save Execution Metadata → Sort Jobs Newest First → Align Field Names → Stamp Processing Time → Cap Batch Volume → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Notion and Gmail aligned by hand for integrations
- Pushing integrations events into Notion and Gmail the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Integrations work where "Probe Endpoint A" is still a manual step before Notion
- Integrations work that only reaches Notion when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Notion and Gmail in step for integrations, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Notion or Gmail are skipped, across all 32 nodes of this integrations build
- A failed Notion or Gmail call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 32 nodes in this integrations build
- Branches rejoin before Notion, so a integrations run reports once rather than 32 times
- Every integrations run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Notion

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

'Already Alerted?' uses cross-execution dedupe specifically so a service that's down for an hour pages on-call once, not on every scheduled probe — alert fatigue is a real failure mode, and this node is the guard against it.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a third endpoint to probe and watch the Merge node's input count update.
2. Point a probe at a URL that returns 500 and confirm exactly one page fires, not one per scheduled check.
3. Change the alert dedupe key so alerts re-fire daily instead of once per incident.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole integrations payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your integrations process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
